artifact: A2 fresh provider admission, isolated staging, and measured launch readiness

blocking_findings: Fresh admission and isolated staging pass, but the canonical measured execute path has no production remote transport to the staged four-GPU instance and no real Owner-local measured input manifest.

Reserve admission incorrectly reuses the 40-hour initial-admission floor at the matched barrier instead of deriving the remaining-work floor from the frozen runtime projection plus its six-hour reserve.

overall.one_line_summary: The AP audit conclusion is well supported: staging passes without measurement, while measured LO remains blocked pending the remote transport and reserve-checkpoint repair.
strengths: The clean pushed-HEAD bundle and metadata-only deployment package validate against the current canonical closure.
Instance 47700074 passed fresh v2 admission and isolated staging with zero GPU/A2 workers and a live watchdog.
All four model roots and supporting A1/runtime assets are already uploaded and hash-validated.
weaknesses: The canonical execute command launches a local subprocess although the required CUDA devices and models are remote.
No production Owner-local measured input manifest exists, and the staged extraction is not a Git worktree capable of validating tracked measurement authority provenance.
The matched barrier cannot pass the current reserve admission after consuming the projected matched critical path, even though the full workload quote remains within the USD 35 hard stop.

strengths: The review binds pushed-HEAD receipts, provider admission, remote stage, adoption, process counts, watchdog state, and the exact executor launch path to the readiness decision.
The required IM work is expressed as executable pass/fail obligations for transport, provenance, input manifest, TTL derivation, and fail-closed tests.
weaknesses: The real Owner-local measured input manifest cannot be independently assessed until IM materializes it.
suggestions: Bind the next AP review to the exact manifest hash and remote synthetic transport receipt.

strengths: The audit limits its conclusion to engineering launch readiness and explicitly denies measured, Selection, Final, and publication authority.
The evidence chain from local-subprocess behavior and remote CUDA placement to the NEEDS_IM route is direct and traceable.
weaknesses: The checkpoint TTL value is a derived target that still requires canonical implementation and regression tests.
suggestions: Have IM emit the exact frozen inputs and formula used for the reserve-checkpoint TTL.

strengths: Failed stage probes, the self-matching process check, resumable ARM-02 transfer, and the launch blockers are preserved rather than hidden.
weaknesses: No remote measured transport alternative has yet been validated, which is appropriate for AP but leaves implementation choice open.
suggestions: Record rejected transport approaches in the IM handoff if they materially affect recovery or provenance.

strengths: Frozen candidate membership, evaluator semantics, protected boundaries, budget hard stop, watchdog, checkpoint, and aggregate-safe receipts remain intact.
weaknesses: Measured execution is not reproducibly launchable on the admitted host until remote transport, tracked provenance, the real input manifest, and checkpoint TTL logic are implemented.
suggestions: Complete audit 006 through IM and require a short AP launch-readiness review before creating measured authority.

findings.target_entity: operational executor, measured adapter, remote staged root, and measurement authority provenance
findings.evidence_locator: src/myis_research/armindex/a2_operational_executor.py execute path; src/myis_research/armindex/a2_measured_adapter.py CUDA/device validation; Owner-local stage receipt b6e690226b572e350686201315d561f9215626500f0e80e59c50abf22efa50bb
findings.observation: The orchestrator starts the production adapter on its own host, while the validated four-GPU runtime and models are on Vast. The staged remote root is not a Git checkout and no real measured input manifest is present.
findings.reasoning: Creating a measured authority or starting LO before a canonical remote transport exists would either fail closed or risk executing on the wrong host, invalidating runtime and provenance bindings.
findings.suggestion: IM implements a narrowly scoped hash-bound remote measured transport, materializes the real Owner-local manifest, validates only synthetic/non-measured transport, and returns to AP before LO.

findings.target_entity: reserve-admit TTL policy and frozen runtime projection
findings.evidence_locator: control/budgets/a2-execution-readiness-v1.json runtime_projection; control/runbooks/A2_PER_ARM_AUTOINDEX_EXECUTION_V1.md matched barrier; src/myis_research/armindex/a2_execution_readiness.py provider admission floor reused by reserve-admit
findings.observation: Initial admission requires 40 hours and the same 40-hour floor is reapplied after the projected 17.92-hour matched critical path. The frozen full critical path is about 26.87 hours with a six-hour reserve.
findings.reasoning: A second 40-hour floor at the matched barrier makes the planned continuation unreachable within the already admitted workload, while a deterministic unfinished-work floor of about 14.95 hours preserves the frozen runtime reserve and USD 35 hard stop.
findings.suggestion: IM separates initial and checkpoint TTL validation, deriving the checkpoint floor from the frozen unfinished reserve critical path plus the existing six-hour reserve, with focused fail-closed tests.
